reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space E with d=dim_R(E)>0, every everywhere differentiable f:E->R, real eta,beta,ell,eps and points x0,xp, assume eta,beta>0,ell>=2,0<eps<=1/2,actual gradient beta-Lipschitz, norm(x0-eta grad f(xp)-xp)<=sqrt(d eta), and64 beta(sqrt(d(ell+log(1/eps)))+ell+log(1/eps))<=1/eta. No convexity is assumed. Set g=grad f(xp),h=x0-eta g,P=(z->sqrt(eta)z)_*stdGaussian(E),nu=Lebesgue restricted to(0,1] product P,q=(z->h+sqrt(eta)z)_*stdGaussian(E). Define W(x,(t,v))=min(1,max(-1,< (pi/2)(cos(pi*t/2)(x-h)-sin(pi*t/2)v),g-grad f(h+sin(pi*t/2)(x-h)+cos(pi*t/2)v)>)), with circular pi. Set m(x)=integral W(x,a) dnu(a),qhat=q.tilted(m). First form q0=(z->x0+sqrt(eta)z)_*stdGaussian(E), then target pi=q0.tilted(-f). The input omega is an iid sequence of attempts(X_n,K_n,(Z_ni)_i,U_n), with independent q,Poisson2,nu^Nat,and uniform[0,1] components. Acceptance B_n means U_n<=product over i in Fin K_n of(1+W(X_n,Z_ni))/2; division is inside each factor and empty product=1. Output Y is X at the least accepting index,or x0 if none accepts. The ENNReal count C=1+sum_n K_n*indicator(all i<n reject) includes all counts through the successful batch, with one initial unit rather than one per trial. The eighteen conclusions are: Y measurable; Y_*rho=qhat;rho(all trials reject)=0;rho,qhat,pi probability;pi<<qhat andqhat<<pi;the actual real RN ell-powers are Bochner integrable under their denominator measures;their corresponding real integrals I=integral((dpi/dqhat).toReal)^ell dqhat andJ=integral((dqhat/dpi).toReal)^ell dpi are both strictly positive;I,J<=1+eps^2;log(I)/(ell-1),log(J)/(ell-1)<=eps^2;the nonnegative expectation of C<=ofReal(1+2exp2);and for every real0<p<=1/2,rho{ofReal([2(exp1-1)(exp2+1/log2)+1+1/log2]*log(2/p))<C}<=ofReal(p). ell is real,not necessarily integer. The cost threshold inequality is strict; cost and probability bounds use ENNReal.
